info.name: Marriage Hall & Hotel Booking (Go)
info.description:
166 endpoints, generated from the routes registered in the Go source by scripts/gen_postman.py.

Getting started:
1. Start the API: `make start`
2. Auth > Create Auth Register Vendor  (creates a venue owner)
3. There is no mail service, so read the OTP from the log:
   `make otp`  ->  set it as the `otp` collection variable
4. Auth > Create Auth Register Verify Email
   This stores accessToken / ownerToken automatically.
5. Facilities > Create Facilities  (stores hallId)

Tokens and ids are captured by test scripts, so most requests work without copying anything by hand. Access tokens last 1 hour; run Auth > Create Auth Refresh when you get a 401.

The payment webhook needs an HMAC signature over the raw body, keyed with PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET from .env - see README.

exec: // An environment value wins: scripts/postman_run.py passes a
// pre-verified identity in that way, and regenerating one here
// would leave the tokens it also passed pointing at a different
// +91 then 10 digits, to satisfy the phone format check.

Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token, since access tokens last 1 hour.

The refresh token ROTATES: the response carries a new one and the old is dead on arrival. Store both. Replaying a spent refresh token is treated as theft and revokes every session for that user.

item.name: Facilities (unified) (4)

request.description:
Creates a hall or a hotel - `type` decides which, and which of the type-specific fields apply. Requires a vendor business (see PUT /api/v1/vendors/me).

amenityIds takes amenity CODES (PARKING, AIR_CONDITIONING, CATERING...) rather than row ids - GET /api/v1/amenities lists them. An unknown code is 400 AMENITY_NOT_FOUND, and one scoped to the other facility type (a hotel breakfast on a hall) is 400 AMENITY_TYPE_MISMATCH, rather than being silently dropped.

Also accepts multipart/form-data, which is how the listing form submits: a `data` part holding this JSON, `amenityIds` repeated once per checkbox, and `images` file parts. Uploads are stored and served by the API; the first becomes the cover.

Captures facilityId, and hallId or hotelId, for the folders that follow.

request.description: Public browse, paged and filterable by type, city and free text.

Side-by-side comparison of 2-3 venues, for the Compare Venues screen. Public.

`ids` is a comma-separated list. Duplicates and more than 3 are rejected; a well-formed id that does not exist gives 404 rather than silently comparing fewer venues than asked for.

PRICES ARE NOT NORMALISED. A hotel quotes per night and a hall per event day, so each venue carries `price.unit` and the response carries `comparablePrice: false` when they differ. Dividing one into the other would make a 4,500 hotel look ten times cheaper than a 50,000 hall.

`missing` lists what a venue does not publish - half the hotels have no price and 16 of 43 halls no capacity - so the client renders a dash, never a zero. `amenities` is the union of all venues' amenities with a per-venue flag, and `distanceKm` is nil for any pair where either venue has no coordinates.

item.name: Marriage Halls (4)

request.description: Halls only - the same listing as /facilities?type=MARRIAGE_HALL.

One hall, with amenities and images. `startingPrice` is its base price per day.

The detail fields also come grouped for the venue screen: `location` (city, state, country, fullAddress, latitude, longitude), `rating` (value, reviewCount), `price` (amount, currency, period - DAY for a hall) and `coordinates`. Each amenity carries an `icon` derived from its code. The flat fields are unchanged and still sent, so nothing built against them breaks.

`price` and `coordinates` are null rather than zero when the venue has no price or was never geocoded - a (0,0) pin would land in the Atlantic.
Updates the marriage hall record. Send the full object, not a partial one.

item.name: Facility Media (9)

request.description:
Uploads an image file (form-data, drag and drop into the Body tab). Stored in S3 and served from there.

**Compressed server-side**: the long edge is capped at 1920px and it is re-encoded as JPEG q=82, which takes a typical 3-8MB phone photo under ~300KB. Done here rather than in the browser because anything can POST to this endpoint - a client-side resize is a courtesy, not a guarantee.

The type is read from the file's bytes, not its name: a .png that is really HTML is rejected. JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF up to 10MB (WebP and GIF are stored as-is - Go has no encoder for them).

The first image on a facility becomes the cover.

item.name: Bookings (5)

request.description:
Books a hall for one date and slot. The price is computed server-side from the hall and any pricing rules - an amount in the body is ignored.

The slot is claimed with a conditional insert, so of two simultaneous bookings exactly one wins and the other gets 409 SLOT_TAKEN. Send `idempotentKey` to make a retry return the original booking instead of creating a second one.
Books rooms for a date range. Priced per night per room type; inventory is decremented per night, so an oversell is rejected.
Lists booking data. See the response fields for the full shape.
One booking. Visible to the customer who made it and to the facility owner.

What the booking will cost, without creating it - the numbers behind the Review Booking screen: hall price, service fee, taxes, total, plus availability and the cancellation tiers.

Nothing is written and no slot is held, so availability is true as of this moment only.

item.description: Creating and managing bookings. Needs hallId or hotelId, and a customer token. Prices are always computed server-side.

item.name: Quotes & Negotiation (15)

request.description:
A customer asks the owner for a price: event type, dates, guest count, budget range. Starts the negotiation and captures quoteId.

Takes `startDate`/`endDate` and `startTime`/`endTime`, the same shape a booking takes - an accepted quote converts straight into one, so the range agreed here is the range that gets booked and charged. `endDate` may be omitted for a single-day event. The old single-date `eventDate` is still accepted, and is echoed back alongside `startDate` so existing clients keep working.

{
  "facilityId": "{{hallId}}",
  "eventType": "Wedding Reception",
  "startDate": "2027-01-15",
  "endDate": "2027-01-16",
  "startTime": "18:00",
  "endTime": "23:00",
  "guestCount": 450,
  "budgetMin": 250000,
  "budgetMax": 400000,
  "specialRequirements": "Vegetarian catering and a stage for the sangeet",
  "preferredContact": "PHONE"
}
